parameters.notes: Guitar amp (the panel calls the effect Guitar Amp; Darkface 65 (US) is its first model). 16-byte block. Byte 0 = model: the wheel on the MODEL selector sent 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 and changed nothing else in the block; names by number from the Zen Go, where each model was loaded by name: 0 Darkface 65 (US), 1 Top30 (UK) Bright, 2 Modern (US) CH3, 3 Plexi 59 (UK), 4 Rock 22.10 (UK), 5 Rock 75 (UK), 6 Marcus II (US) Lead, 7 Tweed Deluxe (US), 8 Overange 120 (UK), 9 BurnSphere (DE) Lead, 10 Bass SuperTube VR. Byte 15 = output level, signed, -48..12 (panel shows 0 dB at raw 0), swept to both ends. Knobs, one notch only (+2), probed while the model was 1 (Top30: Volume, Top Cut, Treble, Bass from left to right): byte 8 at the Volume position, byte 7 Top Cut, byte 5 Treble, byte 2 Bass; the Darkface picture at load agrees for Volume (raw 89, pointer near 8.9) and Bass (62). Their ranges were not captured: the sweep ran after the model sweeps had left the model at 10 (Bass SuperTube VR), whose panel has its knobs elsewhere, so the four knob sweeps sent no frame. Bytes 1, 3, 4, 6, 9-14 (other models' knobs and switches; default 46 .. 3f 00 .. 00 .. 00 01 00 00 00 00) are unidentified. Only model and output are mapped; every other byte would be written back unchanged. NOT EDITABLE: no cat 0x07 read of this effect has been captured, so its read layout (and whether its index is the type) is unknown and the app never writes a block it could not read first. The 2026-11-22 vendor panel run confirms there is none to capture: with the amp loaded (model Top30) the panel was closed and reopened, sent no cat 0x07 request on connect or when the rack opened, and showed its own default model Darkface 65; panel 1.9.22 keeps effect settings only in its own model. read_stride / read_offset are left out on purpose. Fields appended after Output (Bright, Gain, Bass, Middle, Treble, Presence, Volume, Volume 2, Switch 2, Switch 3, Switch 4, Switch 5): ported from the Zen Go, not captured on this device. They were mapped from vendor-panel captures on the owner's Zen Go (same effect type and block); the value meanings below are copied from the Zen Go note: Bright: 1 = lever up on Darkface 65; other models use this byte for their own switch (see below). One block for all models; which knob a byte is depends on the model (names as printed, by byte): Darkface 65: Bass 2, Middle 3, Treble 5, Volume 8, Bright 10. Top30: Bass 2, Treble 5, Top Cut 7, Volume 8. Modern CH3: Gain 1, Bass 2, Middle 3, Treble 5, Presence 7, Volume 8, byte 10 = 0 Raw / 1 Vintage / 2 Modern. Plexi 59: 2, 3, 5, Presence 7, Volume 8. Rock 22.10: Pre-amp Volume 1, 2, 3, 5, Presence 7, Master Volume 8. Rock 75: Gain 1, 2, 3, 5, Presence 7, Volume 8. Marcus II: Drive 1, 2, 3, 5, Master 8, Volume 9, Shift (treble/drive) 11, Shift (bass/middle) 12, Normal/Bright 13, Off/Deep 14. Tweed Deluxe: Tone 3, Volume 8, Normal/Bright 11. Overange 120: HF Drive 1, Bass 2, F.A.C 3, Treble 5, Gain 8. BurnSphere: Gain 1, 2, 3, 5, Presence 7, Volume 8, Normal/Bright 10, Off/Bottom 11. Bass SuperTube: bass 2, midrange 3, treble 5, volume 8, bright 10, ultra-hi 11, 1-2-3 = byte 12 (0-2), bass-cut/off/ultra-low = byte 13 (0-2). Bytes 4 and 6 moved on no model. A model change rewrites only byte 0. These fields supersede the "only model and output are mapped" statement above. Settings read on this device, 2026-11-22: loaded through this project into the channel 3 rack, the cat 0x07 reply was 01 00 46 3e 3f 00 44 00 32 59 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 01 .. (one flag byte, then the 16-byte block the load wrote, 17 bytes per instance), so the effect is editable here although the vendor panel itself never reads it.
